Bug_Title: NP: Method may return null, but is declared @Nonnull (NP_NONNULL_RETURN_VIOLATION)
Bug_Details:
This method may return a null value, but the method (or a superclass method
which it overrides) is declared to return @Nonnull.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the getNonNullString method, which is annotated with @Nonnull but can return null when the parameter returnNull is true.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBugReturnsNull method calls the showBug method with the parameter set to true, which triggers the bug in the getNonNullString method. Since getNonNullString is annotated with @Nonnull but returns null when returnNull is true, this causes a violation of the @Nonnull contract, leading to a failed assertion in the test.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that both tests passed without any assertion failures. The second test, which is expected to trigger the bug by checking for a null return value, did not fail. This suggests that the bug, although present in the code according to the bug rule, was not triggered or detected by the test execution.
